answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that is slashed for proven fraud, like a falcon's hunting license revoked after one bad kill. New identities start with a thin layer of trust, shale-like: cheap to join but worthless for high-value work until they build a verifiable history of honest trades. Reputation accrues slowly, like basalt cooling into solid rock, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes and a thousand histories. An attacker pays linearly for every fake voice, while honest agents compound trust for free.
